title.narrative: Giving for Change programme - Uganda

description.narrative:
The aim of Giving for Change – funded by the Dutch government’s ‘Power of Voices’ programme – is to foster local giving as an expression of voice, civic participation, solidarity and dissent. The programme will build evidence around new thinking, approaches and leadership that support community philanthropy development.
Giving for Change will promote community philanthropy as a strategy for achieving community-led development by increasing local ownership, buy-in and claiming of rights, and by challenging the notion that development is something that is “done to” communities by external actors.
Against a global background of shrinking civic space, Giving for Change will encourage civil society organizations, including and especially human rights organizations, to value and adopt local resource mobilization as a form of constituency building, and as a way to strengthen their position as legitimate champions and defenders of diverse causes, with strong roots in the communities they serve.
#ShiftThePower. While the programme will maintain an explicit focus on strengthening rights and claiming capacities of communities in relation to public government structures, another dimension of it relates specifically to challenging power dynamics, and establishing more equitable practices within the international development system itself.
Programme activities will include action research, trainings and grants to stimulate local giving, which will be led in each country by national anchor institutions. The role of consortium members will be to help “weave” dialogue, learning and exchange across the programme itself, as well beyond to global platforms and audiences as part of larger advocacy and influencing efforts to transform development and philanthropic practice.

The programme in Uganda will seek to change the situation of citizens in Uganda with interventions aimed at not only changing their attitude towards giving as a form of expression and dependence on external funding but also how they approach/carryout activities in their everyday lives. To do this, both the citizens, their organisation (CSAs), private sector, government and international/development partners need to make a number of adjustments, at personal and institutional levels. This change must be in mindset, programming, funding models and regulation inter alia. The contributions from the different partners that need to be engaged will collectively have to make contributions including but not limited to space, time, coordination, expertise, technical backstopping inter alia.

1. UNNGOF partnered with a CoP for youth participation and empowerment (Open Space Centre) to conduct a week's long philanthropy debate symposium. It attracted 180 young people from 11 African countries to engage in rigorious intellectual discussions, improve their debating skills, and participating the future of african philanthropy. There was demonstrable appreciation for the wealth that Africa possesses which had over the years benefitted a few, at the expense of the larger community. The debators challenged policymakers (who were present) to enact laws that enhance the potential of Local Philanthropy in ensuring gender responsiveness and equitable distribution of resources. 2. Parish Development Model (PDM)-Aimed at fast tracking government implementation, reviewing its effectiveness, making recommendations, and securing commitments from government actors. 3.The Grand bargain country level meeting: This was aimed at improving the quality funding-25% of donor allocation to local actors and harnessing the power of quality partnerships between donors and local actors (Master-servant relationship).

For example: 1.RETE-Uganda had a fundraising campaign to meet the basic needs of elders in their areas of jurisdiction.2. As witnessed from 6 testimonials and a video story, in West Nile and Kigezi - Practices were changed from 'waiting for the goverment to act' to initiating community mobilisation drives. The practices that changed were around social accountability, in the sectors of roads &infrastructure, education, and finance. We anticipate that these practices will ultimately inform by-laws and laws respectively.

In December, 2024, UNNGOF commissioned 2 studies; a comprehensive scan on the legal and policy framework for the philanthropy sector in Uganda and revenue collection practices and their impact on Local Economic Development. The outcomes of these studies will be instrumental in shaping engagement with policy-makers at local and national levels to facilitate a shift in policies which will improve government and powerholder accountability towards communities, respect for human rights, and increase gender inclusiveness.

5 trainings were conducted with 208 Individual CSAs representing CSOs (103 males, 105 females): 1 documentation and story-telling training, 1 capacity building training with media practitioners, and 3 physical LFR and MS trainings.The spike in performance from 60 to 208 was because of increased turn up of participants as a result of the relevance of the content in the current context of dwindling funding and dynamicism in the donor funding trends.

As part of membership servicing and efforts to build a society that recognizes, respects and harnesses the power of local philanthropy. Participants were not only enlightened on the value of local fundraising but also equipped with skills and approaches to make it work. Consequently, follow-ups are made to find out the trainees progress in implementing their fundraising plans.

title.narrative: # of CSA actors involved in CoPs

description.narrative: # of CSA actors involved in CoPs

comment.narrative: All baseline values of this programme are set at 0

908 CSAs of which include100 women led, 110 youth led actively participated in the dialogues and fireplace conversations with leadership of the 5CoPs. The increased rate of achievement was because of change of implementation approach for the national level engagements - the change involved a bottom-top approach of engaging with the LED policy through the 14 regional fireplace conversations and 7 regional LED dialogues, of which, each activity attracted atleast 15 and 40 participants per activity. See the details below: The CoPs co-convened the Local Economic Development(LED) conversations with District LED committees (7 dialogues). These discussions facilitated a reflection on how community philanthropy can support the implementation of the LED policy in Uganda. These insightful reflections triggered appreciation of the vast untapped wealth within districts, that required coordinated efforts to tap this potential. Likewise, there was commitment to constitute and activate district LED Committees.

description.narrative: # of CoPs mobilized

comment.narrative: All baseline values of this programme are set at 0

Continoued working with the same CoPs reported from previous years, In the course of the year, the CoPs played an active role in a number of events. 1. One of the members of the CoPs, PAC-Uganda conducted roadshow civic rights empowerment meetings in markets and trading centres, across 6 districts in Teso sub-region, eastern Uganda, reaching 5,039 people (2,992 males, 2,047 females). 2. In the spirit of building a social movement that harnesses the potential of Community philanthropy, the CoPs identified reliable media practitioners from across the country. UNNGOF organised a 2-days media symposium to create a harmonised understanding of the meaning and practice of Community Philanthropy. These are instrumental in shining a spotlight on local philanthropy, shaping narratives, and influencing social change in Uganda. Ultimately, UNNGOF plans to partner with a reputable institution to recognise and celebrate media practitioners who actively contribute to this goal.3.The CoPs spearheaded the mobilisation and facilitation of the LED conversation across the sub-regions.

The same 5 CoPs identified in previous years underwent a training on documentation and story-telling, as a result, we have witnessed more publications of stories on their website, use of social media and active participation on diverse media outlets. Additionally, they participated in reflection meetings to share lessons learnt as peers - this has resulted into commitments to replicate best practices, for example, RIAMRIAM is set to replicate the NGO information centre model of WECISNET with modifications. This further strengthens collective efforts towards community philanthropy.

3 CSOs were recorded to have increased constituencies. Reason for the variance: There was a 6-month implementation pause due to leadership transition which affected our momentum building for the philanthropy social movement that we are working with. Consequently, we shall fast track the documentation of the CSA contributions in the first 6-months of 2025.

Due to multiple trainings on the importance of philanthropy by UNNGOF and the CoPS, more CSAs are contributing in kind, time and cash. This is evident in qualitative statements in the mid term review report and success stories collected by UNNGOF teams. For example; 1.PAC has a social enterprise that was funded by C-fund(a media campaign van that is hired by both state and non-state actors(UNNGOF IPs follow-up survey report), 2. RETE-Ug a constituent of WECISNET(One of the UNNGOF partners) has received donations in voluntary time- communities are responsive to their calls-for-action. 3.WECISNET launched an NGO information centre and hired a compliance officer as a result of the P4D trainings and mentorships.
